response.answer:
Quarter 3 in this course is Semester 2: Quarter 3 [1], which covers Units 9–12. The Quarter 3 column of the course summary table lists the "Preparing for Tomorrow's Workplace Skills" tasks for the quarter [2][3], and they are detailed in the unit key assignments:

Unit 9 – Motivating Employees (Preparing for Tomorrow's Workplace Skills): Decide whether you are motivated more by intrinsic rewards (satisfaction, sense of accomplishment) or extrinsic rewards (money, bonuses), and explain. Then interview friends and classmates to find out what motivates them and discuss differences in perspective (Interpersonal, Information); submit to Google Classroom using the provided Graphic Organizer. A related Team Activity has teams of three to five students act as the management team of a start-up with limited resources but a need for a motivated, skilled workforce, brainstorming motivators other than large bonuses and high salaries and presenting findings to the class [4].

Unit 10 – Operations Management (two Preparing for Tomorrow's Workplace Skills tasks): (1) Use Google to search "supplier information," visit several firms' websites (e.g., Walmart, Northrop Grumman, Verizon), compare the requirements they set for suppliers — how they differ and how they are similar — and create a comparison chart with sources cited. (2) Pick a small business in your community, list the resources critical to its production and operations, interview the owners digitally or in person, consider what would happen if those resources became unavailable, then discuss supply-chain management strategies in small groups and present solutions (Resources, Information, Interpersonal) [5].

Unit 11 – Products and Pricing (Preparing for Tomorrow's Workplace Skills): Pick a product you use frequently (cosmetic/toiletry, snack food, clothing, book, computer program, video game), identify its target market and whether the company's marketing strategy reflects it, then consider the broader product category and how the product or marketing strategy could be adjusted to appeal to other market segments (Systems). Related "Using the Net" work: read marketing articles and visit the American Marketing Association site, then pick a marketing technique and explain its appeal in a reflective journal in Google Classroom [6].

Unit 12 – Distributing and Promoting Products: take Quiz #6 on twenty core concepts from Units 11 & 12, analyze how a regularly used product is marketed across media/promotions/publicity against the six promotional goals and your own response as a target consumer, and complete the "Working the Net" supply-chain-management and global-logistics research presentations [7].

Also introduced at the start of 3rd quarter is the FINAL, "Your Career in Business" [8], whose Part 1 personal reflection questions ask how you can enhance your interpersonal skills [9], why learning to plan matters in school and the real world [10], which school-developed skills transfer to professional life [11], what strategies help you find, keep, and advance in your dream job [12], and what key attributes employers look for in interviews [13]; it is submitted as a written report and 5-minute video presentation [14].
